subject: TTFT & live-stream behavior — recap, targets, and cadence proposal
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivers <alex.rivers@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + ask: TTFT & live-stream behavior follow-up

Hi Alex / Sam —

Thanks for the call this morning — quick recap and a concrete ask so we can size the pilot and lock in SLA targets. Happy to iterate if anything below is off.

What we heard you want (summary)
- User experience target: interactive assistant feels instantaneous for short prompts; acceptable slightly longer TTFT on long generations.
- Preferred streaming: bi-directional updates from client (you indicated you need client-sent cancel/feedback), so WebSocket is currently favored.
- Peak sizing: you mentioned high-volume periods around market open, but we need concrete concurrency/QPS to finalize autoscale and cache sizing.

Proposed baseline SLOs (engineering recommendation)
- TTFT (1st token emitted) target: 250 ms for short prompts (<= 40 tokens pre-gen), 400–600 ms for longer prompts (>= 200 tokens) under typical load.
- Streaming chunk cadence: 120–250 ms pacing with chunk sizes ~0.5–3 KB (depends on tokenization); we recommend pacing over fixed token counts to smooth user experience.
- Concurrency/throughput assumptions for pilot: 100 concurrent active WS sessions, peak 250 RPS.

What we need from you (asks)
1) Confirm expected sustained concurrency and absolute peak RPS during market-open windows.
2) Share a small sample of representative payloads (1–3 example prompts and expected length in tokens).
3) Confirm you prefer WebSocket (bi-directional) vs SSE (unidirectional) for the final integration.

Next steps we propose
- Engineering pilot (2 weeks): validate TTFT on a staging mirror of production traffic; collect perf traces.
- Canary rollout with 5% traffic and autoscale rules based on observed packet pacing.
- Post-pilot: commit to either Dedicated pool or Hosted with reserved bursts depending on peak.

I attached a short SLO table and a brief doc on streaming options. If helpful I can also map these numbers to cost estimates for a 3-month pilot.

Proposed demo: Thu 21 May 10:00–11:00 PT or 15:00–16:00 PT — tell me which slot works.

Thanks,
Ava

Subject: Re: Recap + ask: TTFT & live-stream behavior follow-up

Ava — thanks, useful recap. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Concurrency: our realistic sustained concurrency during trading hours is ~80–120 active websocket sessions (concurrent editors), with short peaks to ~300 RPS for burst queries (orders of magnitude lower outside market-open).
- Average prompt sizes: most prompts are short (10–60 tokens), but we do have sets that hit 180–350 tokens for summaries.
- WebSocket preference: yes, we need bi-directional to ship in-session feedback/cancellation. SSE would be acceptable for read-only workflows, but not our primary use case.

We can share a set of 5 representative prompts (anonymized) by EOD.

Accept the pilot plan in principle — would like the 2-week engineering pilot and a canary. Also, we want to see the TTFT distribution (p50/p90/p99) during the pilot, not just averages.

Demo slot: Thu 21 May 15:00–16:00 PT works for Sam + me.

Alex

Subject: Re: Recap + ask: TTFT & live-stream behavior follow-up

Thanks for the notes — a few technical clarifications and concrete mitigations we can run in pilot: 

1) WebSocket vs SSE: agree WebSocket for your use case. We'll enable WS with a lightweight keepalive and an explicit cancel frame to reduce wasted compute on long generations.

2) TTFT levers we will exercise:
  - Prefix/KV cache: pre-prime common system prefixes (we'll ask for typical prompt prefixes during onboarding). This often reduces cold TTFT by ~40–60 ms.
  - Packet priming: send a tiny warm-up request immediately after connection (0.5–1 KB) for sessions that expect to go interactive. We'll use sampling to limit cost.
  - Model selection + quantization: for short prompts recommend a faster variant (same model family, lower latency quantized variant) to meet 250 ms p50.

3) Measurement plan (pilot): we'll report p50/p90/p99 TTFT, chunk cadence distribution, and chunk sizes observed. Also CPU/GPU utilization and queuing metrics.

4) Concurrency: given your 80–120 sustained concurrency, our suggested pilot capacity is 150 concurrent WS sessions to allow headroom; peak RPS cap 350 for simulated market bursts. If you need guaranteed tail latency we should consider a Reserved Dedicated pool.

I'll attach a short ops playbook for how we'll run the measurements and the JIRA ticket we'll use to track infra changes.

- Aditya
